heading: EXT. FLOATING MARKET OF BELLS - DUSK

units.text: EXT. FLOATING MARKET OF BELLS - DUSK
A market built on rafts lashed together across a slow green river, each stall hung with a thousand tiny bells that ring in the evening wind.
Lanterns drift on the water.
The air tastes of cinnamon and wet rope.
At the center of the flotilla, a single raft has gone quiet.
Its awning sags.
Its bells hang unmoving, as though holding their breath.
ILSEBETH CROWE, 40s, in a coat stitched from sailcloth, stands at its edge with a long pole.
Across the water-gap, a smaller raft drifts nearer, poled by TALLIS ARVEN, 20s, barefoot, his hair full of salt.
Steady. Steady.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: She braces.
The raft thumps against hers.
Tallis catches a rope and ties it off with the careless speed of one who has done it ten thousand times.
Evening, Captain.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: Not Captain anymore.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: That's not what the river says.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: The river doesn't say anything.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: It says plenty. You just don't listen.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: She turns to the crowd gathered on the neighboring decks.
Fishwives, tinkers, a juggler stilled mid-toss, a child on a father's shoulders.
All watching.
Good people of the Bells. A word.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: The crowd murmurs.
A bell somewhere rings once, and falls silent.
The river is dropping. Six inches since dawn. The old channel closes in three days.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: Gasps.
Someone drops a basket.
We can wait for rain. Or we can leave tonight.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: A woman near the front calls out.
Ilsebeth lifts a hand.
No. I won't ask you to follow me. I'll ask you to choose.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: She turns, back to Tallis, and lowers her voice.
Did the ferrymen come?
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: Yes.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: How many?
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: Nine. They'll tow us as far as the weir.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: And past it?
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: Past it, we're on our own.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: She nods.
Looks at the water for a long time.
Then she looks up at the awning where the bells hang motionless.
Strange. They always ring when I lie.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: Maybe you're not lying.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: Maybe I'm not.
units.name: ILSEBETH

units.text: She lifts the pole.
Sets it against the planks.
Pushes.
Across the market, one by one, the ropes are cast off.
The bells begin to ring, a slow wave that runs along the whole flotilla, lantern to lantern, raft to raft, until the entire river sings.
There it is.
units.name: TALLIS

units.text: Ilsebeth does not smile.
But she stands straighter, and her hands, on the pole, are steady.
